definitions.explanation: Trees with needle-like or scale-like leaves, typically cone-bearing. Most are evergreen.

examples.japanese: {松|まつ}や{杉|すぎ}は{針葉樹|しんようじゅ}です。
{針葉樹|しんようじゅ}は{寒|さむ}い{地域|ちいき}でも{育|そだ}ちます。
examples.english: Conifers can grow even in cold regions.

examples.japanese: {針葉樹|しんようじゅ}の{森|もり}は{一年中|いちねんじゅう}{緑|みどり}です。
examples.english: Coniferous forests are green all year round.

notes:
{針葉樹|しんようじゅ} refers to trees with needle-like leaves.

{針|しん} = needle, {葉|よう} = leaf, {樹|じゅ} = tree

Common Japanese conifers:
- {松|まつ} (pine)
- {杉|すぎ} (cedar)
- {檜|ひのき} (cypress)
- {樅|もみ} (fir)
- {唐松|からまつ} (larch - a deciduous conifer)

Characteristics:
- Most are evergreen (except larch)
- Bear cones ({松ぼっくり|まつぼっくり} for pine cones)
- Needle-like leaves reduce water loss
- Softwood, used for construction

Opposite: {広葉樹|こうようじゅ} (broadleaf trees)
